featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a very popular Malavni & Kokani cuisine  restaurant  in Lalbaug area.
It is popular for its fresh seafood,Mutton & chicken dishes.
It follows thali system.
Ambiance  is simple & ethnic,comfortable seating,fully air-conditioned . There are two restaurants with different decor but same menu separated bya spectacle shop.
Service is friendly,but sometimes can be very slow as restaurant is full most of the time.Waiters are well dressed & courteous.
Restaurant is very clean & follows good hygiene.
Their menu has a few seafood,Mutton & chicken starters.
Then different varieties  of thalis.
We had specially gone there to have good fresh seafood but found the rates too high as they were as per size.
A Surmai orpomfret thali at around 1000/- however big the fish sounds too high so we had to skip them.
We had a Prawn thali which was tasty with vade & had fried prawns not very big,prawn masala,fish curry,sol kadi,vade & rice for 550/- which was good & tasty.
Also had a Mutton thali with vade for 550/- which was also tasty & worth the price having mutton masala,mutton masala ,sol kadi,vade,rice.
On the whole it was a good meal except for the high pricing of fish items. No rice dishes like biryanis are available  on the menu which is also disappointing.
Can visit with family when in lalbaug area.

featured_reviews.review_text:

It’s not exactly pure Malvani or Konkani cuisine, but more of a fusion with Vidarbha-style flavors, which actually makes it stand out. Every dish has a homely yet rich taste that leaves you wanting to try more.
The atmosphere is lively and comfortable perfect for families or groups. The interiors have a simple, rustic charm and the overall vibe makes you feel right at home. What really impressed me was the staff they’re extremely polite, attentive, and always ready to suggest the best dishes based on your taste.
Overall, Majghar is a place that balances great taste, generous portions, and warm service beautifully. Highly recommended if you love traditional Maharashtrian flavours and don’t mind rolling out full and happy!

Visited Malvani Klub Restaurant at Lalbaugh with my wife, and we were genuinely impressed with the food, service, and overall experience. We ordered the Bangda Thali and Prawns Thali, and both were absolutely delicious. The Prawns Fry served as a starter was perfectly spiced and crispy, while the Solkadi was refreshing and authentic.

The Bangda fry in the thali had that perfect Malvani masala flavour, and the curries were rich, aromatic, and truly reminded us of homely Maharashtrian coastal food. The prawns curry was equally flavourful, and the chapatis were soft and fresh.

Apart from the excellent food, the staff deserves a special mention — very polite, friendly, and attentive. They made the dining experience even better with their warm hospitality.

If you love Maharashtrian or Malvani cuisine, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Nitant Pandhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coastal Paradise for Seafood Lovers! 🦀✨
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you are looking for authentic Malvani flavors in Mumbai, Malvani Klub is an absolute gem. We visited recently and were blown away by the freshness of the seafood and the richness of their traditional masalas.

The Highlights:

Starters: We started with the Fried Bombil and Prawns Fry. The Bombil (Bombay Duck) was perfectly crisp on the outside and buttery-soft inside—just the way it should be! The prawns were succulent, fresh, and seasoned to perfection.

The Thali Experience:

Surmai Thali: The fish was a generous size, well-marinated, and paired beautifully with the authentic Malvani rassa.

Chicken Komdi Vade Thali: The vade were fluffy and hot, making them the perfect companion to the spicy, flavorful chicken curry.

Crab Thali: A true standout! The crab was meaty and the gravy had that deep, soulful coastal spice kick.

Kolambi Bhaat: This was a revelation! Fragrant rice cooked with juicy prawns and a blend of aromatic spices. It’s a must-order if you want a hearty, one-pot Malvani meal.

Solkadhi: No Malvani meal is complete without this. Their Solkadhi was refreshing, creamy, and had the perfect balance of kokum and garlic to cleanse the palate.

The food here is amazingly awesome and truly authentic. The portions are satisfying, and the taste reminds you of a home-cooked meal in the Konkan belt. Whether you're a hardcore seafood fan or a chicken lover, this place will not disappoint!

Recommendation: Go hungry, and definitely don't miss the Kolambi Bhaat!

-b. Pomfret: 9/10
-c. Bombil: 7/10

4. Fresh Lime Soda: 8/10

Crab Lollipop wasn't great. I have had better elsewhere.

The thalis were awesome. The fish were very fresh and tasty that it made our day. Surmai was the best. It had the best flavor, followed by Pomfret and then the Bombil. Surmai and Pomfret were rawa fry with little masala. It was just plain batter fry for the Bombil. We make better Bombil fry at home, so yeah.
The rice bhakari tasted awesome when it was hot.
Dry Prawns/Jhinga/Javla tasted good with the bhakari.
The pomfret fish and curry was very fresh and tasty.
Solkadhi was chilled, felt refreshing and tasted good.

Gulab Jamun was the worst. Hard, dry and low on flavor.

Restaurant is smaller compared to the one near kemps corner. Cleanliness was decent. No washrooms. Only a basin is available. No Queue when we arrived at 8pm. But a queue started building later on.

Group of 4. Saturday Dinner. Mid April 2026.

Yes, there’s almost always a long waiting line, and at times you may be asked to share a table with other diners. But honestly, that’s only because the place is packed with people who keep coming back for the food. And once you taste it, you’ll understand why.

The seafood is fresh, flavorful, and cooked to perfection. What makes the experience even better is the value for money. Unlike many places that charge extra for every little thing, the thali here is genuinely generous and unlimited, you can ask for refills of the items in your thali as many times as you’d like.

Great food, excellent portions, and prices that feel justified. If you’re a seafood lover, the wait is absolutely worth it.

Along with that there was kaleji masala (liver gravy) one more fantastic preparation  of assal malvani food. Don't miss having it with kombdi wade(its made of traditional flour mixed and fried nice and fluffy) or ghavne (Rice flour). Along with this all, they will also serve Solkadi (its a drink made of nice blend of wild mangosteen fruits along with some garlic and coriander, its amazing drink) do not miss this.

And to conclued this tasty food have parole (made of Rice flour and grated coconut,sweetened by jaggery with lot of ghee)

You must visit to this place and do try the amazing food of Indian west costline. This place will not disappoint you at all..

Highly recommended for anyone who loves Malvani cuisine. Will definitely visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Subodh Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Hi Subodh, 
Experiencing the flavors of the Konkan coast is truly what dining is all about, and it’s wonderful to hear that our seafood dishes resonated with you. The Bombil Fry and Butter Garlic Pepper Crab are favorites for a reason, and it’s delightful to know they stood out during your visit. Your pro tip about the "Catch of the Day" is sure to help other guests maximize their experience!
Regards, 
Mahesh Lunch Home

featured_reviews.name: Nakul Janglay
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Fresh Catch by Francis recently after hearing a lot about it and honestly came back with mixed feelings.

We tried -

Mushroom Butter Garlic was decent, nothing wrong with it, but nothing memorable either.

Bombil Rava Fry was probably the better dish of the lot. Crispy, tasty, and enjoyable.

Bangda Ambotic Curry was good, but felt like a standard Goan curry. Not something I’d go back specifically for.

Crab Meat Spicy Masala.
It was more like a regular seafood bhurji than a standout crab dish. Now where close to justifying the exorbitant price being charged.

Pomfret Hara Bhara Tawa Fry.
The biggest letdown. The fish didn’t feel particularly fresh, the taste was quite average, and the pricing for a small medium sized portion felt just too steep. For that kind of money (or even less) you can easily get a proper wholesome seafood thali elsewhere.

Overall, the food wasn’t bad, just pretty underwhelming for the pricing and hype. Maybe Goan flavors are intentionally subtler and my palate leans more towards Konkani/Malvani seafood.

If I’m spending that kind of money on seafood in Mumbai, places like Nav Chaitanya and Gajalee still set the benchmark for me in terms of flavor, consistency and value.

It's a restaurant that serves a vast array of seafood items and some standout dishes that are worthy of being called Legendary.

The dishes I ordered during my visit were Bomblivi fish fry, Prawn Rechada and a bowl of Mixed Sea food pulao.
Add to that, 2 mugs of kingfisher beer to help in aiding the food down the stomach correctly.

The outcome, i was absolutely in wonderland after gorging on their food like there was no tomorrow.

The Prawn Rechada was simply outstanding to another level. The flavours, reminding me of the coastal beaches of India really gave an everlasting taste to hook onto.

The mixed seafood pulao was again another real dish that was crafted amazingly by their chefs. The homemade spice aromas were so imminent that it wasn't a surprise about finishing up the dish by myself.

Overall service and management deserves a 5/5. Food deserves a 5/5 as well .

Surprisingly, the bill still included charges for the sushi as well as service charges. Upon bringing this to their attention, the staff quickly removed those charges. However, they should not have been added in the first place, given the situation.

One positive takeaway was the politeness and courteousness of the staff, who handled the issue without hesitation. Despite this, the combination of portion concerns and an unfortunate hygiene lapse made this an experience we wouldn't eagerly return for.

As a self-proclaimed seafood addict, I was in heaven. I sampled a wide range of dishes, each bursting with flavor and freshness.

The Tom Kha Soup was a fragrant and comforting start. The Prawns Butter Garlic were perfectly cooked and incredibly flavorful. The *Yellow Chili Prawns  packed a delicious spicy punch. The Surmai Masala Fry was a classic done exceptionally well. The Thalasseri Clams were a fiery delight, showcasing the flavors of Kerala. The Rawas Gassi was a rich and creamy Mangalorean-style curry. The Neer Dosa and Appam were the perfect accompaniments to soak up the delicious gravies.

But the real surprise was the Sitaphal Tricones Holige! This innovative dessert was a delightful fusion of Indian and modern flavors. A must-try!

Overall:
Bharat Excellensea is a must-visit for any seafood lover in Mumbai. The restaurant offers a wide variety of fresh, flavorful dishes with influences from across India's coastal regions. The recent revamp has enhanced the dining experience, making it a perfect spot for a special occasion or a memorable meal. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Mast Malvani – A Hidden Gem in Lalbaug for True Malvani Flavours
📍 Located near Currey Road, Lalbaug, Mumbai

If you’re in search of authentic Malvani cuisine in Mumbai, you’ll know that many places fall short when it comes to delivering real flavors. But hidden in the heart of Lalbaug lies Mast Malvani, a modest eatery that truly lives up to its name. With over 2000+ reviews and a solid 4.3 rating, we decided to finally give it a try—and we’re glad we did!

---

Ambience & Experience

The restaurant is small, with just about 5 tables, seating around 30-40 guests at a time. Despite the size, their management is top-notch. We were given a wait time but seated within 15 minutes. What’s smart? They take your order while you wait, so your food hits the table almost as soon as you sit down. Efficient, right?

---

What We Ordered

🐟 Surmai Thali

A generous piece of Surmai Fish—choose between Rava Fry or Green Masala Fry (both were phenomenal, each with its own distinct coastal kick).

Served with Konkani-style fish curry, Javla (dry shrimp), Solkadi, your choice of Bhakri / Wade / Amboli, and rice.

Every bite screamed authentic Malvani coastal soul food.

🍗 Chicken Thali

One bowl of rich and spicy Malvani Chicken Masala

Another bowl of comforting Malvani chicken gravy

Accompanied with Bhakri, Solkadi, and a signature Malvan-style chutney that stole the show.

The spice, flavor, and balance were spot on.

---

Must-Try: Solkadi

We've had Solkadi across Mumbai, but this one? Truly refreshing, authentic, and soothing. You’ll want seconds.

---

Final Verdict

Whether you're craving a satisfying thali or want to go à la carte, Mast Malvani delivers on all fronts — taste, speed, hospitality, and affordability. It’s no-frills but full-on flavor.

💰 Super pocket-friendly
⭐ Perfect for solo meals, family dinners, or food trails
📍 If you’re around Lalbaug, Currey Road, or even just nearby — don’t miss this spot.

Mast Malvani is not just another Malvani restaurant. It’s THE Malvani restaurant you’ve been looking for in Mumbai.

In addition to the culinary delights, the prices at Mast Malvani are refreshingly reasonable, making it accessible to a wide range of diners. For the quality of food and service provided, it's an absolute steal.

All in all, Mast Malvani is a hidden gem that deserves to be discovered by food enthusiasts far and wide. Whether you're a fan of Malvani cuisine or simply looking to embark on a gastronomic adventure, this establishment is a must-visit. featured_reviews.name: Gaurav Biswas
featured_reviews.review_text:
Waited for 15 minutes to get a place.
They serve all sorts of packet Chaknas here like Moong Dal, Chakli, Seng, Chana, Roasted Chana Etc. These are all reasonably priced between 20 to 40.

We order Bombil Fry, Chicken Sukka, Kori Rotti and Neer Dosa & Solkadi
Being married to a Mangalorean and been a regular to Mangalorean outlets back in Kudla I know the taste very well. This was nowhere near sadly. The Bombil Fry being a Maharashtrian special was just oil fried with light red batter rather than Rawa Fry. Killed the appetite completely unfortunately. It was served a small bowl of Coconut gravy which was again very bland.

The Chicken Sukka was too bland. Quantity was ample but the taste was honestly bland. I tried to finish it with the Neer Dosa since Bhakri wasn't available.

Neer Dosa again was served with a small bowl of Coconut gravy as usual bland.

The Kori Rotti being a staple food amongst mangaloreans was a major let down. It didn't have any flavor and even had sasive(Mustard) in it which was unlike of any Mangalorean Outlet. My wife finished it with a lot of difficulty.

The only savior was the Solkadi and it was really tasty and thick. It was too good and cheap at the same time.

Overall verdict is it's a cheap and pocket friendly place. The food was 2/5. Drinks are probably cheap since everyone was busy consuming that. Solkadi 6/5. The staff were always on the feet and ready to attend.

featured_reviews.name: Makarand Sainis
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent Seafood restaurant in Mumbai. A very old mangalorian style seafood restaurant which also offers other non veg and veg dishes.

Food quality is exceptional. Very tasty food with least spices. Portions are quite sufficient.

Must try Butter Garlic Prawns and Butter Garlic Crab here. Also, Pomfret, Surmai, Bombil (Bombay Duck), crabs, lobsters are very very good and very tasty.

Do not miss out chicken Makhani (Butter Chicken). One of the finest butter chicken I had in years.

Service is very quick, servers are very polite and helpful.

Seating capacity is less (26 tables, max 100 guests) and restaurant is always full. So, make sure you book table in advance before coming to Trishna for Lunch or dinner.

featured_reviews.name: Dan Liu
featured_reviews.review_text: I’m baffled by the popularity of this place. The garlic butter crab was decent, but that was about it. The biryani was lukewarm, the butter chicken tasted more like sweat than usual, and the Bombay duck was nothing special. Despite these shortcomings, the place is clearly popular, as you can feel the rush to seat the next customer. This place was highly recommended, but it didn’t live up to the hype.

featured_reviews.name: Anagha Surve
featured_reviews.review_text: Seafood lovers this is ‘The Best’ experience you will ever have. Lots of options in appetisers and the seafood is fresh and cooked to perfection. Tried their Singaporean Crab it was lip-smackingly good. Their pomfret and prawns dishes are also lovely. Quantity and portions are good.

featured_reviews.name: Shantanu Dey (Sandy)
featured_reviews.review_text: Without doubt one of the best seafood joints of Mumbai. We had their best selling ‘crab butter garlic’ which is always awesome. This time we also tried the Hyderabadi rawas tikka suggested by our steward. With subtle tastes of masala this was great too! Didn’t have space for any dessert. Prices are on the higher side and so is the experience.

featured_reviews.name: rushda moulvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Trishna truly lives up to its reputation. In my opinion, it’s one of the best seafood restaurants in Mumbai.

The prawn ghee roast is exceptional. Even though I’m not usually a big fish lover, their Schezwan fish and biryani are absolutely delicious. The seafood is extremely fresh with no smell at all.

Also love their butter naan and cheese naan. A special mention to the staff extremely professional, friendly, and attentive.A must-visit for anyone coming to Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Shreyas Nair
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely Amazing Seafood, Really nice food but quite pricey. Must visit if you’re in the area and want to have some seafood. We visited for dinner and spent 2.5k per head.
Here are our recommendations:
Tiger butter garlic prawn 10/10 MUST HAVE
Pomphret ghee roast - 9/10 can try the prawn ghee roast as well
Neer dosa - really good
Appam - this was a miss, not as good as Kerala Appam
Coorg promphet curry - A really nice coriander based curry to have with rice or bread

featured_reviews.name: Monika Lobo
featured_reviews.review_text:
We ordered the chicken hot and sour soup—it was amazing. The butter garlic dish was also great and price was 3,900/- for large crabs and small size is for 1900/- but they don’t serve it, it’s just on the menu. The prawns were just okay. Unfortunately, the Rawas fish tikka was very bad and fish was very hard and we informed the team as well ; I would not recommend ordering it. Do try the chicken haryali—it’s really good.

Total bill was 8,200/-

It’s only for tourist

featured_reviews.name: Lawrence W
featured_reviews.review_text: Worth the hype! Seafood is my personal favorite and this place satisfied my cravings. Loved the “medium” prawns (they were massive!) and fish curry with neer dosa! Seafood biryani was great too. On the pricer side but definitely a nice place to treat yourself, will be back for more!
